text:
ops_tom: Obs: We're seeing a persistent GPU scheduling backlog in eu-central3 since 11:03 UTC. Autoscaler is creating nodes but kubelet register latency is high (~90s) and many pods stay Pending. Queue depth ~600 active requests, P95 latency for jobs up 3-4x. Raising incident.
oncall-bot: Alert: gpu-provisioning-delay-eu-central3 fired at 11:05 UTC — severity: high. Incident created INC-1234. Pager duty routed to oncall.
eng-sre-jen: Can you paste the scheduler logs + controller-manager? suspect CNI update caused pod network teardown. Any recent node image changes?
ops_tom: No image changes since yesterday. Here's tail of kube-scheduler logs: ```W1123 11:08:21.123 scheduler_cache.go:547] failed to assign: networkAttachErr: timeout waiting for cni plugin``` and `kubelet` showing: `failed to register node: dial tcp 10.0.0.1:10250: i/o timeout`
support_lead: We're getting multiple support escalations — especially from enterprise customers on Dedicated. Need a status page update and ETA for customers. Can ops give a customer-facing ETA? @maria_support please collect top 5 affected orgs.
maria_support: Collected list: AcmeCorp, FinLeap, DataShip, HealthGrid, EduAI. All reporting degraded inference latency >10s. I've opened priority tickets and CC'd customers.
alex_infra: Short-term mitigation: shift traffic from eu-central3 to eu-west2 using traffic-router rules, but that will increase latency for EU customers (+30-80ms) and cost for burst. We can script a gradual shift to keep caches warm.
eng-sre-jen: Agree. Also suggest evicting low-priority preemptible batches in eu-central3 to free GPUs for latency-critical jobs. We can set `priorityClass` changes and `kubectl delete jobs -l batch=preemptible` to accelerate.
ops_tom: Executed manual eviction of 28 preemptible jobs at 11:22 UTC. Started scaling up eu-west2 pool and running `traffic-router --shift region=eu-west2 --percent=30 --dry-run=false` to move 30% of new sessions. Monitor: /incidents/1778882345/metrics
support_lead: Draft status page update (please review): ```Investigating: We are currently experiencing GPU provisioning delays in eu-central3 causing increased latency and request queuing for some customers. We are shifting traffic to eu-west2 and evicting low-priority work to restore capacity. ETA for majority restoration: 45-90 minutes. We will post updates every 15 minutes.``` :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
eng-sre-jen: Two followups: 1) Add note about potential increased costs for customers on Dedicated while traffic is routed. 2) Add link to support ticketing for enterprises. Also we should enable fallback to a lower-cap quantized model for some orgs — patching rollout now.
maria_support: Notified customers with the draft and requested permission to publish. AcmeCorp asks for an explicit ETA; CFO of FinLeap requested live updates on Zoom — assigning account exec.
ops_tom: Current metrics: queue depth down from 600 -> 340 after evictions and initial shift. Node registration RTT still high (~45s). Working with cloud provider on network fabric investigation (ticket #CLOUD-7890). Provider says they are investigating a control plane flapping issue.
oncall-bot: Update: page:INC-1234 state->investigating at 11:40 UTC
support_lead: Publishing status page now. Use this exact text for publish: ```Status: Degraded performance in eu-central3. Mitigation: Traffic shift to eu-west2 and eviction of non-critical workloads. ETA: 45-90 minutes for majority restoration.``` Please include link to support form: https://support.redwood.ai/incident/INC-1234
alex_infra: Running gradual shift to 60% now to speed recovery while monitoring tail latency. Expect short-lived spikes as KV caches warm.
eng-sre-jen: After traffic shift, make sure to clear prefix cache to avoid stale responses: `redis-cli -h prefix-cache flushall` for transferred sessions. I'll coordinate with runtime team.
ops_tom: Will update here every 15 minutes. Next checkpoint 11:55 UTC. Thanks everyone.
support_lead: Noted. I'll keep customers updated and escalate any VIP asks to leadership. :thumbsup:
